source_text: ἱερουργοῖς ἐκνενέμηνται κλῆροι, καὶ τούτους αὐτοῖς ἐσαεὶ διασώζεσθαι καὶ ἀναποβλήτους εἶναι προστέταχεν, ἀναγκαίως ἐκεῖνο δηλοῖ. Εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο, φησὶν, ἕνα τῶν ἡγουμένων ἤτοι τῶν ἱερουργῶν, τοῖς ἰδίοις διανεῖμαι τέκνοις ἐξ ἰδίου κλήρου τινὰ, πεπήχθω, φησὶ, τὸ δοθὲν, καὶ ἀνεκποίητον ἔστω τῷ λαβόντι τὸ δῶρον. Οἴχεται γὰρ οὐκ ἐπί τινα τῶν ἀλλογενῶν ὁ κλῆρος, ἀλλ' ἐξ ἱερέων εἰς ἱερούς. Εἰ δὲ δὴ καὶ ἑνὶ τῶν οἰκετῶν χαρίσαιτο, κεκτήσεται, φησὶν, οὐ βεβαίως ὁ λαβὼν, ἀναδραμεῖται δὲ πάντως ἐπὶ τὸν ἡγούμενον, ἐν τῷ ἔτει τῆς ἀφέσεως, ὁ κλῆρος αὐτοῦ. Προσεπιτάττει γε μὴν ἀποσείεσθαι τὸν ἱερουργὸν τοῦ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων ἐφίεσθαι κλήρου, τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ τὸ, οὐ μὴ λάβῃ ὁ ἀφηγούμενος ἐκ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ἆρά σοι γέγονεν ἀποχρῶν ὁ λόγος εἰς τὴν τοῦ πράγματος διασάφησιν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἴτω δὴ οὖν εἰς βάσανον τὴν πνευματικήν· τύποι γὰρ δὴ τὰ ἐν νόμῳ, καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἡ μόρφωσις ἐγκεχάρακται ταῖς σκιαῖς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν κλῆροι μὲν ἀσφαλεῖς καὶ μένοντες, οἱ ἐκ πατέρων εἰς τέκνα, ἀπόβλητοι δὲ καὶ ἀνόπιν ἰόντες, οἱ ἐκ δεσποτῶν εἰς τοὺς οἰκέτας· τοῦτο γὰρ ἔφη τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι. {ΚΥΡ.} Εἷς δὲ ἡμῶν τῶν ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένων καθηγητὴς, ὁ Χριστὸς, κλῆρον ἔχων ἴδιον, τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἔφασκεν, ὅταν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐποιεῖτο τοὺς λόγους ὡς ἐν σχήματι προσευχῆς, ὅτι «Πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ, σά ἐστι, καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμὰ, καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς.» Ψάλλει δέ που καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Μελῳδὸς, ὅτι ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος, ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκε δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· οὓς μὲν γὰρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ, πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, καὶ ᾧ μὲν δέδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως, καὶ τὰ τούτοις ἀδελφά. Καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀγαθοῖς τὰς τῶν ἀγαπώντων αὐτὸν καταπιαίνει ψυχάς. Βεβαία δὴ οὖν καὶ ἐρηρεισμένη τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς τε καὶ ἐλευθέροις τῶν δεδωρημένων ἡ κτῆσις. Τοῖς δὲ τὸ δοῦλον ἔχουσι πνεῦμα, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, τὴν ἐλευθέραν πίστιν οὐ προσιεμένοις, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ ζυγὰ κειμένοις ἔτι τῆς βεβήλου καὶ βδελυρᾶς ἁμαρτίας, ἀπόβλητος καὶ ἀφαιρετὴ καὶ ἡ δοθεῖσα χάρις διὰ Μωσέως, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἡ ἐν νόμῳ γνῶσις, παιδαγωγοῦσα πρὸς ἀλήθειαν. Καὶ κλῆρος μὲν ὅλως μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων οὐδεὶς, μερὶς δὲ οὐδεμία μετὰ Χριστοῦ. «Τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι,» φησὶ, «δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος, καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.» Ὅτι δὲ ἀπόκληρος ὁ Ἰσραὴλ τὴν πίστιν οὐ προσηκάμενος, οὐδὲ τοῖς εἰς ἐλευθερίαν ἀξιώμασιν ἐκλελαμπρυσμένος, διαμεμήνυκεν ὁ Σωτὴρ, τὴν τοῦδε τοῦ νόμου, καθάπερ ἐγῷμαι, δύναμιν παρακομίζων εἰς μέσον. Ἔφη γὰρ ὧδε τοῖς ἀπειθεῖν ἑλομένοις·
pass_a_gloss: [continuing §15: since lots have been assigned to the holy] sacred ministers, and he has ordered these to be preserved for them always and to be not to be cast off, it necessarily shows that: if it happen that one of the leaders, that is, the ministers, distribute something from his own lot to his own children, let the given thing be fixed, and let the gift be inalienable for the receiver. For the lot goes not to one of other race but from priests to holy ones. But if he should grant to one of the household servants, the receiver will not possess securely; his lot will run back altogether to the leader in the year of release. He further orders the minister to shake off aiming at others' lots; this, I think, is 'the leader shall not take from the inheritance of his people'. Is the account sufficient for clarification of the matter? PALL.: Very much. CYR.: Let it go then to the spiritual testing; for the things in law are types, and the form of the truth is engraved on the shadows. PALL.: True. CYR.: So lots from fathers to children are secure and remaining; castable off and going backward those from masters to servants; this the sacred Writing said. PALL.: I understand. CYR.: One leader/guide of us justified in faith, Christ, having his own lot, that of God and Father. Hence he said, making words to him as in form of prayer: John 17:10 quoted. The divine Singer sings: having gone up on high he took captive captivity, gave gifts to men; some he placed in the Church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers; to one a word of wisdom, to another word of knowledge, and the things akin. Simply, with his own goods he fattens/enriches the souls of those loving him. Secure and fixed the possession of things given for ministers and free. For those having the slavish spirit, i.e. those from Israel not admitting the free faith, still lying under yokes of profane and loathsome sin, castable off and removable is even the grace given through Moses, i.e. the knowledge in law, tutoring toward truth. And no lot with saints, no portion with Christ. Saying quoted: to the one having it will be given and abound; from the one not having, even what he seems to have will be taken. That Israel is lotless, not admitting faith, not made brilliant with the dignities unto freedom, the Saviour declared, bringing into the middle the power of this law, as I think. For he said thus to those choosing to disobey:
pass_b_english: Cyril: …ministers, and he has commanded that these be kept for them forever and never be lost, the passage must mean this. For if it should happen, he says, that one of the leaders, that is, of the ministers, gives part of his own lot to his own children, let what was given stand fixed, he says, and let the gift never pass away from the one who received it. For the lot does not pass to someone of another race, but from priests to those who are consecrated. But if he gives it as a favor to one of his household servants, the one who received it, he says, will not hold it securely; his lot will surely return to the leader in the year of release (Ezekiel 46:17). He further commands the minister to put away any desire for the lots of others; for this, I think, is the meaning of ‘the leader shall not take any of the inheritance of his people’ (Ezekiel 46:18). Has the account been enough to make the matter clear to you?
Cyril: Then let it be put to the spiritual test; for the things in the law are types, and the shape of the truth is engraved in the shadows.
Cyril: So the lots that pass from fathers to children are secure and lasting, but those that pass from masters to servants can be lost and go back again; for this is what the sacred Scripture said.

Cyril: Now we who have been justified by faith have one leader, Christ (Matthew 23:10), who has as his own lot that of God the Father. That is why he said, when he addressed him as if in the form of prayer, ‘All that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified in them’ (John 17:10). And the inspired Singer sings somewhere that, having ascended on high, he led captivity captive and gave gifts to men (Psalm 68:18; Ephesians 4:8). For some he placed in the Church, first apostles, second prophets, third teachers (1 Corinthians 12:28); and to one is given a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge (1 Corinthians 12:8), and the gifts akin to these. In a word, he enriches the souls of those who love him with his own good things. Secure, then, and firmly founded is the possession of these gifts for those who are both ministers and free. But for those who have the spirit of slavery (Romans 8:15), that is, for those of Israel, who do not accept the faith of freedom but still lie under the yoke of profane and loathsome sin, even the grace given through Moses can be lost and taken away; that grace is the knowledge in the law, which leads like a tutor toward the truth (Galatians 3:24). They have no lot at all with the saints and no portion with Christ. ‘For to him who has,’ he says, ‘more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from him who has not, even what he seems to have will be taken away’ (Matthew 25:29; Luke 8:18). That Israel is left without a lot, since it did not accept the faith and has not been made glorious with the honors that belong to freedom, the Savior made plain, bringing forward, as I think, the force of this very law. For he spoke thus to those who chose to disobey:

choices.english: from priests to those who are consecrated
choices.why: ἐξ ἱερέων εἰς ἱερούς rendered 'from priests to those who are consecrated' (sons of priests).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: Opens mid-sentence, continuing Cyril's turn from §15 ('assigned to the holy…'). ἐξ ἱερέων εἰς ἱερούς rendered 'from priests to those who are consecrated' (sons of priests). 'Types… shape of the truth… in the shadows': possible echoes of Romans 2:20 (μόρφωσιν… τῆς ἀληθείας ἐν τῷ νόμῳ) and Hebrews 10:1 (σκιάν), left uncited as Cyril's stock formula. Matthew 23:10 cited for εἷς… καθηγητής, ὁ Χριστός (verbal match). Psalm quotation: LXX Psalm 67:19 = English Psalm 68:18; Cyril's form ἔδωκε δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις follows Ephesians 4:8, not the LXX ἔλαβες δόματα ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ, so both are cited. 'Some he placed in the Church' follows 1 Corinthians 12:28 wording (Ephesians 4:11 is close but not the source). 'Grace given through Moses' may echo John 1:17 (uncited). 'No lot with the saints, no portion with Christ' may echo Acts 8:21 and Colossians 1:12 (uncited). The saying 'to him who has' combines Matthew 25:29 (δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται) with Luke 8:18 (ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν). Section ends with a colon introducing the quotation of John 8:34–36 in §17.

review.method: translate from the Greek, then a separate clause-by-clause review against the Greek
changes: τὸ δοθέν / τὸ δῶρον / ἀνεκποίητον: 'let what was given stand fixed ... let the gift never pass away from' (inalienable, not 'taken')
ὡς ἐν σχήματι προσευχῆς: restored 'as if' (Cyril's christological hedge)
τὴν ἐλευθέραν πίστιν: 'the faith that makes free' (added agency) -> 'the faith of freedom'
Causal participles οὐ προσηκάμενος / οὐδὲ ἐκλελαμπρυσμένος attached to ἀπόκληρος correctly

Scripture checked: Ezekiel 46:17-18, Matthew 23:10, John 17:10, Psalm 68:18 (LXX 67:19) + Ephesians 4:8 (Cyril's wording = Ephesians), 1 Corinthians 12:28, 12:8, Romans 8:15, Galatians 3:24, Matthew 25:29 + Luke 8:18 all confirmed
